claim: Persistent hash-index manager on a build-heavy repeated-session semi-join: measured speedup 7.078x.
kind: single-system ablation (xlog against its own baseline)

provenance.gpu: NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe, GPU-bdb502b0-1852-1504-5cd0-cafd7908b7e7, driver 580.159.04, 81920 MiB
provenance.note: recorded by the pod session that produced this file. The device UUID and CPU model are read from the triangle-counting artifact of that same session, which is the only file of the run whose runner records them; the environment probe of the run records the GPU name, driver and CPU quota directly.

harness.raw_line: persistent_hash_index_perf left_rows=8 right_rows=8000000 join_repetitions=1 warmup=12 iterations=9 cached_median_sec=0.002273627 uncached_median_sec=0.016093291 speedup_ratio=7.078 cached_output_rows=8 uncached_output_rows=8 cached_builds=1 cached_hits=12 uncached_builds=0 cached_dtoh_calls=0 cached_htod_calls=0

build_profile.caveat: this fixture was measured in a DEBUG build. An earlier version of this file recorded the command with a --release flag the run did not use; the flag is removed here. The ratio is therefore not comparable with a release-mode measurement, and the index-rebuilding arm is the one a debug build penalises most, so 7.078x is an upper bound pending a release re-run.

harness.gate: the test asserts the ratio against a >=1.5x target and prints the raw medians; the gate lives at persistent_hash_indexes in crates/xlog-core/src/config.rs (env XLOG_PERSISTENT_HASH_INDEXES)

limits.dispersion: the harness emits only a median per arm, so this fixture carries no dispersion at all
limits.equivalence: the arms are compared on output row count, not on the row set
